messages:
luis-telemetry: heads up — we started seeing a big drop in child spans for /api/generate around 09:12 UTC. parent spans OK, but most DB/http children missing. 60%+ drop in span count for that service window.

sophie-oncall: confirmed in the oncall dashboard, looks correlated with a deploy to the ingress proxy at 09:10. linking logs now.

kevin-platform: that was a small rollout of proxy-sanitizer v2 (scrubs headers with a ruleset). it was intended to remove PII headers only. did we accidentally add trace headers to the ruleset? :grimacing:

anna-engineer: i pulled the nginx config from the new image, there's a lua sanitizer that does a regex over header names and then `ngx.req.clear_header(k)` for matches. ruleset file: `headers_disallow: ["^x-.*", "^x-forwarded-.*", "traceparent"]` — oops `traceparent` explicitly listed.

mira-observability: that would explain it — if `traceparent` or `baggage` got cleared at the edge then everything downstream can't correlate. can we see an example request where header missing?

luis-telemetry: grabbed a raw tcpdump from pod before rollback. original client sent: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01` then nginx delivered upstream with header absent.

kevin-platform: deploy-bot initiated an automatic canary rollback because error budgets tripped. deploy-bot: `rollback proxy-sanitizer v2 -> v1 (canary failed: tracing loss)`

deploy-bot: rolled back `proxy-sanitizer` to v1 at 09:16 UTC. canary traffic now back to v1. :white_check_mark:

anna-engineer: i've patched the ruleset to use anchored regex for PII keys only and removed `traceparent`/`baggage` from the blacklist. pushed a hotfix to the image with tests that assert `traceparent` header preserved.

mira-observability: good. we should also add an e2e that runs a simple trace through the ingress and asserts parent/child visibility in our tracing pipeline before promoting. linking a quick GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/issues/423

luis-telemetry: follow-ups: 1) confirm retention/exporter didn't drop buffered spans during the window, 2) run a replay if possible, 3) add an alert for sudden parent->child span ratio deviation. anyone want ownership?

sophie-oncall: i'll own 1 and 3 — checking exporter queues now. initial look: collector had elevated retries to our cloud-exporter from 09:12–09:17 with transient 502s, but no large backlog; most spans eventually exported.

kevin-platform: i'll own 2 — if the buffered spans never contained children we can't replay missing children. but if they exist on the collector we can re-ingest. i'll check the collector store and retention snapshots.

mira-observability: i'll PR the ingress e2e and the span-ratio alert. suggest a simple PromQL alert: `sum(child_spans)/sum(parent_spans) < 0.6` over 5m for service="api-generate".

anna-engineer: added the lua unit test and a CI check to validate header pass-through. PR incoming.

luis-telemetry: thanks all. quick retrospective note for the rollout UX: can we gate sanitizer rule changes behind an integration test that validates OpenTelemetry headers passthrough? this bug was invisible until production.

kevin-platform: yep — will add gating in the release pipeline so header-scrub rules trigger the ingress e2e. also adding a deploy note that any header removal must be explicitly reviewed.

sophie-oncall: closing the incident for now since rollback restored traces and there's no data loss detected so far. re-open if collector backlog shows missing children. :v:
